issue.title: Create constructor for file-file network graph from Depends

labels.name: type:enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: module:file_network
labels.description: Issues related to *file* network construction, parsing and metrics.

issue.body:
# 1. Setup for Depends

 * It's a java project, so it requires JDK, but nothing else.
 * Download the **release** (not the source!!) here: https://github.com/multilang-depends/depends/releases/tag/0.9.6a (I will use version 0.9.6.a). 
 * That's it. 

# 2. Usage 

I will use the .sh script instead of the java -jar interface available on the downloaded depends folder. The required input is the .src code of a project (hence can just use the .git for perceive input). The command goes as follows:

`./depends.sh cpp ~/Desktop/kaiaulu_project_input/apr apr --dir="/tmp/" --auto-include --granularity="file" --namepattern="/" --format="json"`. Breaking down from left to right:

 * language (no auto-detect apparently, had to use the browser on github to see language %) : `cpp` 
 * the input source code folder: `~/Desktop/kaiaulu_project_input/apr`
 * the name of the output file (no extension), any name goes but I will convention the project name: `apr`

Everything else are optional flags, and in fact most are already the default parameter. However, for sanity sake I'd rather have them explicit even if default, in case it changes in the future:

 * output folder (will use tmp):  `--dir="/tmp/"`
 * include all paths (I assume we should use this?):  `--auto-include`
 * dependency granularity: `--granularity="file"` 
 * file paths are defined by "/" instead of ".": `--namepattern="/"` 
 * output expected by the R code to load from /tmp/ will be .json: `--format="json"` 

# 3. Some considerations on reproducibility 

Insofar, the only really immutable files need to be the `.git` folder of the project, and the `.mbox`. Surely we could keep a .gitlog backup, and a .depends backup, and another thousand backup intermediate files, but I'd rather just keep the bare minimum. 

When we move to the time window stage, where the .git repo needs to do git checkouts back and forth, I will check if a git checkout can ruin anything (branches, merges, etc), otherwise, I just need to save the original commit hash to checkout back in the end. 

# 4. Output 

## 4.1 Files
Using `Usage` above, 3 files are output to `/tmp/`:

 1. depends-dv8map.mapping
 2. apr.json

The `depends-dv8map.mapping` file does not seem dependent on the data used as input. For the purposes of file-file network, it is unnecessary.  Hence, the next section focus just on `apr.json`:

## 4.2 apr.json 

Here's an example output trimmed from APT. **The goal is to turn this into an edgelist**. 

```
{
  "schemaVersion" : "1.0",
  "name" : "apr-sdsm",
  "variables" : [ "/Users/cvp/Desktop/kaiaulu_project_input/apr/atomic/netware/apr_atomic.c", "/Users/cvp/Desktop/kaiaulu_project_input/apr/atomic/os390/atomic.c", "/Users/cvp/Desktop/kaiaulu_project_input/apr/atomic/unix/builtins.c", "/Users/cvp/Desktop/kaiaulu_project_input/apr/atomic/unix/builtins64.c", 
`...`],
  "cells" : [ {
    "src" : 208,
    "dest" : 149,
    "values" : {
      "Import" : 1.0
    }
  }, {
    "src" : 339,
    "dest" : 142,
    "values" : {
      "Import" : 1.0
    }, `...`
  } ]
}
```

Observe I inserted `...` twice in the file above to abbreviate the long list of file names, and the long list of "cells". 

 1. In essence, the .json file contains two parts: The first list all the `file_names` as a list. For my purposes, this needs to be loaded as a character vector in memory. 
 2. The other part is the dependencies itself, shown on the cells. The `src` and `dest` are the indices from `file_names`. Each cell can be seen as an **edge** of the **edgelist** table. I just need to use `file_names` to substitute the indices by the file names as each row is extracted. 
 3. The `values` column translate to a `weights` column in the edgelist, as it defines the number of dependencies. Here are some examples from APR on how they can appear:

### 4.2.1 A dependency can have a count higher than 1

```
{
    "src" : 404,
    "dest" : 332,
    "values" : {
      "ImplLink" : 7.0
    }
```

### 4.2.2 There may be multiple dependencies

```
    "src" : 108,
    "dest" : 198,
    "values" : {
      "Call" : 2.0,
      "Import" : 1.0,
      "Use" : 10.0,
      "Parameter" : 1.0,
      "Contain" : 1.0
    }
```

To keep the function flexible, I plan to parameterize it's call with a character vector so the user can specify which dependencies should or not be used to calculate the weight. The ones not used get discarded. The ones used get their values summed into a single `dependencies_total`. 

It seems there is a total of 12 different types defined. See `depends-dv8map.mapping` for the possible values.

issue.body:
# Wolfgang MBOX Downloader

```
BASE_URL=http://mail-archives.apache.org/mod_mbox
PROJECT=hbase-dev
FROM=2015
TO=2020

for year in `seq ${FROM} ${TO}`; do
  for month in `seq -w 1 12`; do
     curl -s -I ${BASE_URL}/${PROJECT}/${year}${month}.mbox | \
          grep "HTTP/1.1 404 Not Found" > /dev/null || \
     curl ${BASE_URL}/${PROJECT}/${year}${month}.mbox \
          -o ${PROJECT}_${year}_${month}.mbox
  done
done

cat *.mbox > ${PROJECT}.mbox
rm ${PROJECT}_*.mbox
````


# Perceval Approach 

Mbox: https://chaoss.github.io/grimoirelab-tutorial/perceval/mail.html

The purpose of this issue is to understand how can a dev-file network can be obtained at function granularity. The following links are cues to that. A more organized analysis is done in further comments. 

This file from Codeface employs ctags:

https://github.com/siemens/codeface/blob/e6640c931f76e82719982318a5cd6facf1f3df48/codeface/cluster/cluster.py#L1414

Exuberant Ctags basically is a parser that takes as input a source file (e.g. bla.py) and outputs metadata of functions and other data objects of said source code as another file. Making sense of the metadata file appears to be very confusing, see this question on SO:

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41933837/understanding-the-ctags-file-format

However, Codeface relies on a python library to parse Ctags, making it much simpler. This implementation appears to be very efficient, as it seems to be just a wrapper to a C file that does the parsing (notice the github project hasn't be updated in a long while):

https://github.com/cloggo/python-ctags

Codeface also relies on this VCS python package, which appears to abstract implementations of version control systems (Git, Subversion):

https://github.com/codeinn/vcs

Lastly, I also found out Exuberant Ctags itself has been abandoned, and other project took over forking it since then: 

https://ctags.io/
